# Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Running

Reviewers mostly agree on a short list. Here are the top picks by what matters most to you.

## Top picks

**1. Bose Ultra Open Earbuds: best overall (about $199, down from $299)**
- **Why:** Runner's World's top pick after more than 2,200 logged miles. They don't bounce, they work with hats and glasses, and they leak less sound than most open-ear designs. They have physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-stride than touch controls. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Downsides:** They're only IPX4, so they're not great in heavy rain. Battery lasts about 7 hours per charge. Volume can fall short in loud city traffic.
- **Timing:** Runner's World said in late September that Bose plans to release new open-ear earbuds "within the next month." If you're not in a hurry, wait a few weeks and check whether the new model arrives or this one drops further.
- **Buy:** $199 at [Bose and Best Buy, linked from WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**2. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: best bone conduction (about $125 to $180)**
- **Why:** This is the classic runner's choice, and the one to pick if hearing traffic is your top priority. It gets about 12 hours of battery and is rated IP55. It has physical buttons and USB-C charging, and adds more bass than older bone-conduction models. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- **Downsides:** The neckband can clash with ponytails, hoods, and high collars. Sound is a bit flat for bass-heavy music.
- **Buy:** As of WIRED's listing, it's $125 at REI and Best Buy, compared with $180 list. [Links in WIRED's review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**3. Shokz OpenDots 2: best for long runs and bad weather (about $200)**
- **Why:** WIRED's overall top pick. Battery lasts 10 hours per charge (40 with the case), and it's rated IP57. WIRED's reviewer fully submerged them without problems. They're clip-ons, so the top of your ear stays free for sunglasses or a hat. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Buy:** $200 at [Amazon, Best Buy, or Shokz, linked from WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Value picks

**Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 (list $149).** SoundGuys rates it the best workout earbud for running. It has strong bass for an open-ear design, an IP54 rating, and a detailed EQ. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [Amazon link via SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80 to $104.** This is SoundGuys' budget pick. It uses an ear-hook design and gets 10 hours of battery, an IP55 rating, and multipoint pairing. On price:
- SoundGuys listed it at **$79.99 on Amazon**. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))
- Dealectric reports that code **AFSC20** brings it to **$104 at Soundcore's own store**, down from $129.99. The code applies only to full-price items. That's an affiliate link: [dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- Check Amazon first. It's probably cheaper even with the code.

**JLab Flex Open, about $40.** This is the cheapest way to find out whether you like the clip-on style. Sound is basic, but it's comfortable and stays in place. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

## Quick guide
- **Want maximum awareness of traffic, or already know you like Shokz?** OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Want the best sound and don't mind the price?** Bose Ultra Open, ideally after you see what Bose releases next.
- **Run long, sweat a lot, or run in the rain?** OpenDots 2.
- **On a budget?** Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2.

Prices change often, so check the retailer's checkout for the final price. If you tell me your budget, whether you wear glasses or long hair, and your phone (iPhone or Android), I can narrow this down.
